evidence: Liv. 23.29.7: obstināverant animīs vincere aut morī
terms.comment: Literally “to conquer or to die”: in Livy, the resolve of soldiers whose way home hung on the battle. It says more than the English “winning is everything”.

sources: John C. Traupman, Conversational Latin for Oral Proficiency, cited by printed page; each phrase checked against the searchable text of the book.
